people.current_position: Assistant Professor, Department of Computer Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas

bio.summary: Jisoo Yang is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at UNLV who received a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Michigan in 2010. The research focuses on operating system and architecture support for new memory technologies such as 3D XPoint and 3D NAND. Yang has contributed to the Linux kernel and Xen hypervisor and did processor architecture research at Intel.
notable: Previously processor architecture researcher at Intel

people.current_position: Professor, Department of Electrical Engineering, UNIST; Director, Wireless and Mobile Networking Laboratory (WMNL)

bio.summary: Hyoil Kim is a Professor of Electrical Engineering at UNIST in Korea and directs the Wireless and Mobile Networking Laboratory. Kim earned a BS from Seoul National University in 1999 and an MS (2005) and PhD (2010) from the University of Michigan under Kang G. Shin. Research focuses on AI-empowered networking, 5G/6G, and dynamic spectrum access.
bio.thesis_title: Efficient Identification and Utilization of Spectrum Opportunities in Cognitive Radio Networks

people.current_position: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering, UC San Diego; Ericsson Endowed Chair in Wireless Access Networks; Director, Center for Wireless Communications

bio.summary: Xinyu Zhang is a Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at UC San Diego, holding the Ericsson Endowed Chair and directing the Center for Wireless Communications. Research covers next-generation wireless network architectures and ubiquitous sensing, with emphasis on millimeter-wave networking, metasurface-empowered communications and AI-augmented mobile computing. Zhang earned a PhD at the University of Michigan in 2012 under Kang G. Shin and previously held a faculty post at UW-Madison.
notable: Best Paper Awards: MobiCom 2020, SenSys 2023, SenSys 2026
